title: Grading Trims & Objs | Clo Feature Deep Dive

summary: ```markdown # Grading Trims & Objs | Clo Feature Deep Dive ## Introduction Hi, my name's Phoebe, and I have some great grading updates for all of you. It's super exciting, so let's dive on in and have some fun while we learn. ## Grading OBJ Trims and Buttons Here I have my screen, and as you can see, I have this cute little Clo emblem as my collar's little button. I brought it in as an OBJ trim. The update here, especially for grading, is that now we can grade OBJ trims and buttons, as well as all of your trims and everything. ### Checking if Your Trim is Glued To see how we do that, first off, you have to make sure you glue your trim. There are a few ways to know if your trim is glued. If you select your trim, you can see that the glue bottle is blue. Additionally, you'll notice a mark on your pattern piece; there's a little plus sign. This is new, and the reason we have this mark is so you can grade it. If something is not glued, the glue bottle won't be blue or filled properly. You can click this to turn it off, or you can right-click to unglue it. ### Visual Indicators of Gluing If I zoom out, you won't see the little plus sign on this side, indicating this one is glued, while the other is no longer glued. Don't worry; you can easily glue something again. ### Gluing Your Trim Here's a trick: I always make sure to click the right point on your trim. For this one, because I want to ensure that the center of my trim aligns with the center of the "C," that's my gluing spot. I'll place my cursor right in the center, go to my glue bottle to activate it, and then I'll place it right here. Now it's glued, and you can see the little plus sign confirming it's set. You can always click again to reglue if you need to. If there's anything wrong with the placement, you can always rotate and adjust it as needed. ## Adding Grading Now that it's glued and all set, you can add your grading easily. Just go to your edit grading tool in your grading section within your 2D window. Make sure your pattern pieces already have grading assigned. I've already graded most of my patterns and assigned grading to them. ### Using the Edit Grading Tool Now, all I'll have to do is select my little marker and, using my arrow keys on my keyboard, I'm going to add in that grading. You can also input it through measurements if you prefer. After adding the grading, voila—that's it! ## Grading Buttons and Buttonholes Isn't that great? We can do the exact same steps for our buttons. You don't have to worry about gluing them in; they've already been placed using my button tool. I can just click here and add it in. Again, I’m using my arrow keys to do this easily. ### Copying and Pasting Grading The same goes for my buttonhole; it’s really easy! Don't forget, we have the ability to right-click and copy. You can select multiple buttons at once by holding down Shift, and then you can right-click and paste. You can paste the grading for both X and Y, just X, or just Y. I'm going to do both X and Y, and that's how you can quickly and easily paste all of your grading to multiple buttons and buttonholes. You can hit Ctrl+C to copy and then Ctrl+V to paste. ## Conclusion That's everything! Really cool, right? Thank you so much for watching! If you have any questions, use the comment section below; someone will get back to you, I promise. If you want to learn more about grading, we have many great videos about grading on our channel. Don't forget to like and subscribe, and check everything out. Thanks for watching, and keep having fun in Clo! ```
